ESV.1: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall repay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
ESV.2: If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him,
ESV.3: but if the sun has risen on him, there shall be bloodguilt for him. He  shall surely pay. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
ESV.4: If the stolen beast is found alive in his possession, whether it is an ox or a donkey or a sheep, he shall pay double.
ESV.5: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, or lets his beast loose and it feeds in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best in his own field and in his own vineyard.
ESV.6: “If fire breaks out and catches in thorns so that the stacked grain or the standing grain or the field is consumed, he who started the fire shall make full restitution.
ESV.7: “If a man gives to his neighbor money or goods to keep safe, and it is stolen from the man's house, then, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
ESV.8: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall come near to God to show whether or not he has put his hand to his neighbor's property.
ESV.9: For every breach of trust, whether it is for an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep, for a cloak, or for any kind of lost thing, of which one says, ‘This is it,’ the case of both parties shall come before God. The one whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
ESV.10: “If a man gives to his neighbor a donkey or an ox or a sheep or any beast to keep safe, and it dies or is injured or is driven away, without anyone seeing it,
ESV.11: an oath by the LORD shall be between them both to see whether or not he has put his hand to his neighbor's property. The owner shall accept the oath, and he shall not make restitution.
ESV.12: But if it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
ESV.13: If it is torn by beasts, let him bring it as evidence. He shall not make restitution for what has been torn.
ESV.14: “If a man borrows anything of his neighbor, and it is injured or dies, the owner not being with it, he shall make full restitution.
ESV.15: If the owner was with it, he shall not make restitution; if it was hired, it came for its hiring fee.
ESV.16: “If a man seduces a virgin  who is not betrothed and lies with her, he shall give the bride-price  for her and make her his wife.
ESV.17: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money equal to the bride-price for virgins.
ESV.18: “You shall not permit a sorceress to live.
ESV.19: “Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death.
ESV.20: “Whoever sacrifices to any god, other than the LORD alone, shall be devoted to destruction.
ESV.21: “You shall not wrong a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
ESV.22: You shall not mistreat any widow or fatherless child.
ESV.23: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry,
ESV.24: and my wrath will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall become widows and your children fatherless.
ESV.25: “If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be like a moneylender to him, and you shall not exact interest from him.
ESV.26: If ever you take your neighbor's cloak in pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down,
ESV.27: for that is his only covering, and it is his cloak for his body; in what else shall he sleep? And if he cries to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
ESV.28: “You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
ESV.29: “You shall not delay to offer from the fullness of your harvest and from the outflow of your presses. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.
ESV.30: You shall do the same with your oxen and with your sheep: seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
ESV.31: “You shall be consecrated to me. Therefore you shall not eat any flesh that is torn by beasts in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.

NKJV.1: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and slaughters it or sells it, he shall restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
NKJV.2: If the thief is found breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt for his bloodshed.
NKJV.3: If the sun has risen on him, there shall be guilt for his bloodshed. He should make full restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
NKJV.4: If the theft is certainly  found alive in his hand, whether it is an ox or donkey or sheep, he shall restore double.
NKJV.5: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed, and lets loose his animal, and it feeds in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
NKJV.6: “If fire breaks out and catches in thorns, so that stacked grain, standing grain, or the field is consumed, he who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
NKJV.7: “If a man delivers to his neighbor money or articles to keep, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
NKJV.8: If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought to the judges to see whether he has put his hand into his neighbor’s goods.
NKJV.9: “For any kind of trespass, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, or clothing, or for any kind of lost thing which another claims to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whomever the judges condemn shall pay double to his neighbor.
NKJV.10: If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies, is hurt, or driven away, no one seeing it,
NKJV.11: then an oath of the LORD shall be between them both, that he has not put his hand into his neighbor’s goods; and the owner of it shall accept that, and he shall not make it good.
NKJV.12: But if, in fact, it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to the owner of it.
NKJV.13: If it is torn to pieces by a beast, then he shall bring it as evidence, and he shall not make good what was torn.
NKJV.14: “And if a man borrows anything from his neighbor, and it becomes injured or dies, the owner of it not being with it, he shall surely make it good.
NKJV.15: If its owner was with it, he shall not make it good; if it was hired, it came for its hire.
NKJV.16: “If a man entices a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall surely pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.
NKJV.17: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the bride-price of virgins.
NKJV.18: “You shall not permit a sorceress to live.
NKJV.19: “Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.20: “He who sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD only, he shall be utterly destroyed.
NKJV.21: “You shall neither mistreat a stranger nor oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
NKJV.22: “You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child.
NKJV.23: If you afflict them in any way, and they cry at all to Me, I will surely hear their cry;
NKJV.24: and My wrath will become hot, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
NKJV.25: “If you lend money to any of My people who are poor among you, you shall not be like a moneylender to him; you shall not charge him interest.
NKJV.26: If you ever take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down.
NKJV.27: For that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What will he sleep in? And it will be that when he cries to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
NKJV.28: “You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
NKJV.29: “You shall not delay to offer the first of your ripe produce and your juices. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
NKJV.30: Likewise you shall do with your oxen and your sheep. It shall be with its mother seven days; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
NKJV.31: “And you shall be holy men to Me: you shall not eat meat torn by beasts in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.

NASB.1: 'If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
NASB.2: 'If the thief is caught while breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there will be no bloodguiltiness on his account.
NASB.3: '[But] if the sun has risen on him, there will be bloodguiltiness on his account. He shall surely make restitution; if he owns nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
NASB.4: 'If what he stole is actually found alive in his possession, whether an ox or a donkey or a sheep, he shall pay double.
NASB.5: 'If a man lets a field or vineyard be grazed [bare] and lets his animal loose so that it grazes in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
NASB.6: 'If a fire breaks out and spreads to thorn bushes, so that stacked grain or the standing grain or the field [itself] is consumed, he who started the fire shall surely make restitution.
NASB.7: 'If a man gives his neighbor money or goods to keep [for him] and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is caught, he shall pay double.
NASB.8: 'If the thief is not caught, then the owner of the house shall appear before the judges, [to] determine whether he laid his hands on his neighbor's property.
NASB.9: 'For every breach of trust, [whether it is] for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, [or] for any lost thing about which one says, 'This is it,' the case of both parties shall come before the judges; he whom the judges condemn shall pay double to his neighbor.
NASB.10: 'If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep [for him], and it dies or is hurt or is driven away while no one is looking,
NASB.11: an oath before the LORD shall be made by the two of them that he has not laid hands on his neighbor's property; and its owner shall accept [it], and he shall not make restitution.
NASB.12: 'But if it is actually stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
NASB.13: 'If it is all torn to pieces, let him bring it as evidence; he shall not make restitution for what has been torn to pieces.
NASB.14: 'If a man borrows [anything] from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he shall make full restitution.
NASB.15: 'If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; if it is hired, it came for its hire.
NASB.16: 'If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged, and lies with her, he must pay a dowry for her [to be] his wife.
NASB.17: 'If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money equal to the dowry for virgins.
NASB.18: 'You shall not allow a sorceress to live.
NASB.19: 'Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
NASB.20: 'He who sacrifices to any god, other than to the LORD alone, shall be utterly destroyed.
NASB.21: 'You shall not wrong a stranger or oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
NASB.22: 'You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.
NASB.23: 'If you afflict him at all, [and] if he does cry out to Me, I will surely hear his cry;
NASB.24: and My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall become widows and your children fatherless.
NASB.25: 'If you lend money to My people, to the poor among you, you are not to act as a creditor to him; you shall not charge him interest.
NASB.26: 'If you ever take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, you are to return it to him before the sun sets,
NASB.27: for that is his only covering; it is his cloak for his body. What else shall he sleep in? And it shall come about that when he cries out to Me, I will hear [him], for I am gracious.
NASB.28: 'You shall not curse God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
NASB.29: 'You shall not delay [the offering from] your harvest and your vintage. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
NASB.30: 'You shall do the same with your oxen [and] with your sheep. It shall be with its mother seven days; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
NASB.31: 'You shall be holy men to Me, therefore you shall not eat [any] flesh torn to pieces in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.

WEB.1: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it, or sells it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
WEB.2: If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
WEB.3: If the sun has risen on him, guilt of bloodshed shall be for him; he shall make restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
WEB.4: If the stolen property is found in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.
WEB.5: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten, and lets his animal loose, and it grazes in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.
WEB.6: “If fire breaks out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
WEB.7: “If a man delivers to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it is stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
WEB.8: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out if he hasn’t put his hand to his neighbor’s goods.
WEB.9: For every matter of trespass, whether it is for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one says, ‘This is mine,’ the cause of both parties shall come before God. He whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
WEB.10: “If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no man seeing it;
WEB.11: the oath of Yahweh shall be between them both, whether he hasn’t put his hand to his neighbor’s goods; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
WEB.12: But if it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
WEB.13: If it is torn in pieces, let him bring it for evidence. He shall not make good that which was torn.
WEB.14: “If a man borrows anything of his neighbor’s, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.
WEB.15: If its owner is with it, he shall not make it good. If it is a leased thing, it came for its lease.
WEB.16: “If a man entices a virgin who isn’t pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.
WEB.17: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
WEB.18: “You shall not allow a sorceress to live.
WEB.19: “Whoever has sex with an animal shall surely be put to death.
WEB.20: “He who sacrifices to any god, except to Yahweh only, shall be utterly destroyed.
WEB.21: “You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
WEB.22: “You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child.
WEB.23: If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;
WEB.24: and my wrath will grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
WEB.25: “If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor. You shall not charge him interest.
WEB.26: If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
WEB.27: for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
WEB.28: “You shall not blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
WEB.29: “You shall not delay to offer from your harvest and from the outflow of your presses. “You shall give the firstborn of your sons to me.
WEB.30: You shall do likewise with your cattle and with your sheep. Seven days it shall be with its mother, then on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
WEB.31: “You shall be holy men to me, therefore you shall not eat any meat that is torn by animals in the field. You shall cast it to the dogs.

CSB17.1: “When a man steals an ox or a sheep and butchers it or sells it, he must repay <sup>ⓛ</sup> five cattle for the ox or four sheep for the sheep.
CSB17.2: If a thief is caught in the act of breaking in, and he is beaten to death, no one is guilty of bloodshed. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.3: But if this happens after sunrise, the householder is guilty of bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution. If he is unable, he is to be sold because of his theft. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: If what was stolen — whether ox, donkey, or sheep — is actually found alive in his possession, he must repay double.
CSB17.5: “When a man lets a field or vineyard be grazed in, and then allows his animals to go and graze in someone else’s field, he must repay <sup>[1]</sup> with the best of his own field or vineyard.
CSB17.6: “When a fire gets out of control, spreads to thornbushes, and consumes stacks of cut grain, standing grain, or a field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution for what was burned.
CSB17.7: “When a man gives his neighbor valuables <sup>[2]</sup> or goods to keep, but they are stolen from that person’s house, the thief, if caught, must repay double.
CSB17.8: If the thief is not caught, the owner of the house must present himself to the judges <sup>[3]</sup> to determine <sup>[4]</sup> whether or not he has taken his neighbor’s property. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.9: In any case of wrongdoing involving an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything else lost, and someone claims, ‘That’s mine,’ <sup>[5]</sup> the case between the two parties is to come before the judges. <sup>[6]</sup> The one the judges condemn <sup>[7]</sup> must repay double to his neighbor.
CSB17.10: “When a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to care for, but it dies, is injured, or is stolen, while no one is watching,
CSB17.11: there must be an oath before the LORD between the two of them to determine whether or not he has taken his neighbor’s property. Its owner must accept the oath, and the other man does not have to make restitution.
CSB17.12: But if, in fact, the animal was stolen from his custody, he must make restitution to its owner. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.13: If it was actually torn apart by a wild animal, he is to bring it as evidence; he does not have to make restitution for the torn carcass.
CSB17.14: “When a man borrows an animal from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not there with it, the man must make full restitution.
CSB17.15: If its owner is there with it, the man does not have to make restitution. If it was rented, the loss is covered by <sup>[8]</sup> its rental price.
CSB17.16: “If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged, and he sleeps with her, he must certainly pay the bridal price for her to be his wife.
CSB17.17: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must pay an amount in silver equal to the bridal price for virgins. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.18: “Do not allow a sorceress <sup>ⓓ</sup> to live.
CSB17.19: “Whoever has sexual intercourse with an animal <sup>ⓔ</sup> must be put to death.
CSB17.20: “Whoever sacrifices to any gods, except the LORD alone, is to be set apart for destruction. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.21: “You must not exploit a resident alien <sup>ⓖ</sup> or oppress him, since you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
CSB17.22: “You must not mistreat any widow or fatherless child. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.23: If you do mistreat them, they will no doubt cry to me, and I will certainly hear their cry. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.24: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will be widows and your children fatherless. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.25: “If you lend silver to my people, to the poor person among you, you must not be like a creditor to him; you must not charge him interest. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.26: “If you ever take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him before sunset.
CSB17.27: For it is his only covering; it is the clothing for his body. <sup>[9]</sup> What will he sleep in? And if he cries out to me, I will listen because I am gracious. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.28: “You must not blaspheme God <sup>[10]</sup> or curse a leader among your people. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.29: “You must not hold back offerings <sup>ⓝ</sup> from your harvest or your vats. Give me the firstborn of your sons.
CSB17.30: Do the same with your cattle and your flock. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to me. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.31: “Be my holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal <sup>ⓑ</sup> found in the field; throw it to the dogs.

NLT.1: “If someone steals an ox or sheep and then kills or sells it, the thief must pay back five oxen for each ox stolen, and four sheep for each sheep stolen.
NLT.2: “If a thief is caught in the act of breaking into a house and is struck and killed in the process, the person who killed the thief is not guilty of murder.
NLT.3: But if it happens in daylight, the one who killed the thief is guilty of murder. “A thief who is caught must pay in full for everything he stole. If he cannot pay, he must be sold as a slave to pay for his theft.
NLT.4: If someone steals an ox or a donkey or a sheep and it is found in the thief’s possession, then the thief must pay double the value of the stolen animal.
NLT.5: “If an animal is grazing in a field or vineyard and the owner lets it stray into someone else’s field to graze, then the animal’s owner must pay compensation from the best of his own grain or grapes.
NLT.6: “If you are burning thornbushes and the fire gets out of control and spreads into another person’s field, destroying the sheaves or the uncut grain or the whole crop, the one who started the fire must pay for the lost crop.
NLT.7: “Suppose someone leaves money or goods with a neighbor for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house. If the thief is caught, the compensation is double the value of what was stolen.
NLT.8: But if the thief is not caught, the neighbor must appear before God, who will determine if he stole the property.
NLT.9: “Suppose there is a dispute between two people who both claim to own a particular ox, donkey, sheep, article of clothing, or any lost property. Both parties must come before God, and the person whom God declares guilty must pay double compensation to the other.
NLT.10: “Now suppose someone leaves a donkey, ox, sheep, or any other animal with a neighbor for safekeeping, but it dies or is injured or is taken away, and no one sees what happened.
NLT.11: The neighbor must then take an oath in the presence of the LORD. If the LORD confirms that the neighbor did not steal the property, the owner must accept the verdict, and no payment will be required.
NLT.12: But if the animal was indeed stolen, the guilty person must pay compensation to the owner.
NLT.13: If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, the remains of the carcass must be shown as evidence, and no compensation will be required.
NLT.14: “If someone borrows an animal from a neighbor and it is injured or dies when the owner is absent, the person who borrowed it must pay full compensation.
NLT.15: But if the owner was present, no compensation is required. And no compensation is required if the animal was rented, for this loss is covered by the rental fee.
NLT.16: “If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged to anyone and has sex with her, he must pay the customary bride price and marry her.
NLT.17: But if her father refuses to let him marry her, the man must still pay him an amount equal to the bride price of a virgin.
NLT.18: “You must not allow a sorceress to live.
NLT.19: “Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal must certainly be put to death.
NLT.20: “Anyone who sacrifices to any god other than the LORD must be destroyed.
NLT.21: “You must not mistreat or oppress foreigners in any way. Remember, you yourselves were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
NLT.22: “You must not exploit a widow or an orphan.
NLT.23: If you exploit them in any way and they cry out to me, then I will certainly hear their cry.
NLT.24: My anger will blaze against you, and I will kill you with the sword. Then your wives will be widows and your children fatherless.
NLT.25: “If you lend money to any of my people who are in need, do not charge interest as a money lender would.
NLT.26: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as security for a loan, you must return it before sunset.
NLT.27: This coat may be the only blanket your neighbor has. How can a person sleep without it? If you do not return it and your neighbor cries out to me for help, then I will hear, for I am merciful.
NLT.28: “You must not dishonor God or curse any of your rulers.
NLT.29: “You must not hold anything back when you give me offerings from your crops and your wine. “You must give me your firstborn sons.
NLT.30: “You must also give me the firstborn of your cattle, sheep, and goats. But leave the newborn animal with its mother for seven days; then give it to me on the eighth day.
NLT.31: “You must be my holy people. Therefore, do not eat any animal that has been torn up and killed by wild animals. Throw it to the dogs.

AMP.1: "If a man steals an ox or sheep and kills or sells it, he shall make restitution of five oxen for an ox or four sheep for a sheep.
AMP.2: "If a thief is caught breaking in [after dark] and is struck [by the owner] so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him.
AMP.3: But if the sun has risen, there will be bloodguilt for him. The thief [if he lives] must make [full] restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold [as a slave to make restitution] for his theft.
AMP.4: If the animal that he stole is found alive in his possession, whether it is ox or donkey or sheep, he shall pay double [for it].
AMP.5: "If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed bare or lets his livestock loose so that it grazes in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
AMP.6: "If fire breaks out and spreads to thorn bushes so that the stacked grain or standing grain or the field is consumed, he who started the fire shall make full restitution.
AMP.7: "If a man gives his neighbor money or [other] goods to keep [for him while he is away] and it is stolen from the neighbor's house, then, if the thief is caught, he shall pay double [for it].
AMP.8: If the thief is not caught, the owner of the house shall appear before the judges [who act in God's name], to determine whether or not he had stolen his neighbor's goods.
AMP.9: For every offense involving property, whether it concerns ox, donkey, sheep, clothing, or any piece of lost property, which another identifies as his, the case of both parties shall come before the judges [who act in God's name]. Whomever the judges pronounce guilty shall pay double to his neighbor.
AMP.10: "If a man gives his neighbor a donkey or an ox or a sheep or any [other] animal to keep [for him], and it dies or is injured or taken away while no one is looking,
AMP.11: then an oath before the LORD shall be made by the two of them that he has not taken his neighbor's property; and the owner of it shall accept his word and not require him to make restitution.
AMP.12: But if it is actually stolen from him [when in his care], he shall make restitution to its owner.
AMP.13: If it is torn to pieces [by some predator or by accident], let him bring the mangled carcass as evidence; he shall not make restitution for what was torn to pieces.
AMP.14: "And if a man borrows an animal from his neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while its owner is not with it, the borrower shall make full restitution.
AMP.15: But if the owner is with it [when the damage is done], the borrower shall not make restitution. If it was hired, the damage is included in [the price of] its fee.
AMP.16: "If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he must pay a dowry (marriage price) for her to be his wife.
AMP.17: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must [still] pay money equivalent to the dowry of virgins.
AMP.18: "You shall not allow a woman who practices sorcery to live.
AMP.19: "Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.
AMP.20: "He who sacrifices to any god, other than to the LORD alone, shall be put under a ban (designated) for destruction (execution).
AMP.21: "You shall not wrong a stranger or oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
AMP.22: You shall not harm or oppress any widow or fatherless child.
AMP.23: If you harm or oppress them in any way, and they cry at all to Me [for help], I will most certainly hear their cry;
AMP.24: and My wrath shall be kindled and burn; I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall become widows and your children fatherless.
AMP.25: "If you lend money to any one of My people with you who is poor, you shall not act as a creditor (professional moneylender) to him; you shall not charge him interest.
AMP.26: If you ever take your [poor] neighbor's robe in pledge, you must return it to him before sunset,
AMP.27: for that is his only covering; it is his clothing for his body. In what shall he sleep? And when he cries to Me [for help], I will hear him, for I am compassionate and gracious.
AMP.28: "You shall not curse God, nor curse the ruler of your people [since he administers God's law].
AMP.29: "You shall not delay the offering from your harvest and your vintage. You shall give (consecrate, dedicate) to Me the firstborn of your sons.
AMP.30: You shall do the same with your oxen and with your sheep. It shall be with its mother for seven days; on the eighth day you shall give it [as an offering] to Me.
AMP.31: "You shall be holy men to Me; therefore you shall not eat meat [from any animal] that has been torn to pieces [by predators] in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.
